newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. recommends 6-month renewal of Macedonia force.
newsitem.headline: U.N. recommends 6-month renewal of Macedonia force.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali Friday recommended a six-month renewal of the 1,100-member U.N. force stationed in the former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia but with a phased reduction of 300 troops.

The U.N. Preventive Deployment Force (UNPREDEP) includes a 500-strong Nordic battalion and a 500-member U.S. task force, supported by a 50-member Indonesian heavy engineering platoon, 35 military observers and 26 civilian police monitors.
The force was sent to Macedonia in late 1992 to deter any spread of violence from other parts of the former Yugoslavia.

"Recent developments in the region, and the enhanced international standing of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, have made such a scenario more remote," Boutros-Ghali said in a report to the Security Council.

"Moreover...it has become increasingly evident that the primary threat to the country's stability may come from internal political tensions," he said, alluding to ethnic problems involving the country's large Albanian minority.

"UNPREDEP has accordingly devoted considerable attention to strengthening dialogue between the political forces and has assisted in monitoring human rights and inter-ethnic relations," the secretary-general said.
He recommended that UNPREDEP's mandate should be extended until May 31, 1997, "with a phased reduction of the military component by 300 all ranks by April 1, 1997."

"This timing would allow for the reduction in the force to be fully effected after the severe winter conditions have passed and for the (U.N.) secretariat to undertake the necessary consultations with troop-contributing countries," he added.
